common_symptoms: abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, constipation, diarrhoea, abdominal distension, cardiac arrhythmias, hypertension, urinary retention, peripheral neuropathies, numbness or tingling, burning sensations, seizures, irritability, depression, anxiety, insomnia, hallucinations, paranoia, disorientation
complications: depression, hepatocellular carcinoma, renal dysfunction, recurrent acute attacks
epidemiology: 1 per 500–50,000 people, more common in women (ratio of between 1.5 to 2:1), rare before puberty, typical age for appearance of symptoms is between 18 and 40 years
risk_factors: genetic_predisposition, hormonal factors, certain drugs, excessive alcohol consumption, fasting or dieting, stress, infections
diagnosis_challenges: non-specific symptoms, similarity with other diseases

common_symptoms: constipation || vomiting || poor food intake || delayed gastric emptying
epidemiology: 90% of individuals are asymptomatic, while an estimated 5% experience repeated attacks. Affected individuals usually recover from an attack within days.
